title: Square Acreage From Perimeter
description: Get a square plot's acreage from its perimeter with Square Acreage From Perimeter — fence length to side to acres, in one chain. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a square plot fenced with 1,320 ft of fence (a quarter mile) has 330 ft sides and covers exactly 2.5 acres — the perimeter knew the acreage all along.
quick_answer: Square Acreage From Perimeter turns a square plot's perimeter into its acreage: divide the perimeter by four for the side, square it for the area, convert to acres. Enter the boundary total and read the acreage — for plots easier to walk around than across.
steps_intro: The boundary you can measure holds the area you cannot:

faq: What if the plot is rectangular, not square?
Perimeter alone cannot fix a rectangle's area (long thin and square share perimeters, not areas). Measure one side too — then the Rectangular Lot Acreage Calculator finishes it.

Part of the boundary is a river or road?
The perimeter is the total boundary as deeded, whatever it runs along. Measure the legal boundary, not the walkable one, if they differ.
Fences often sit a margin inside the true line. For acreage, the deeded boundary governs; the fence is a clue, not the title.
Why does the square maximise area?
For fixed perimeter, area peaks when all sides equalise — a rectangle 660 × 0 holds nothing; 330 × 330 holds the most the same fence can enclose.
Deeded area is plan (horizontal) area. A hillside's fence runs longer than its plan perimeter — survey figures, not slope figures, feed this calculator.
